decisions.reason: The ID Vault was launched with fanfare in 2023 and is a low-cost feature tied to the core identity platform, so management will carry it while results remain uncertain, even though a mere feature could later be folded silently into the super-app offering.

The identity-bound wallet is only mentioned and overlaps with the dedicated payment and wallet framework (Product D), making it a candidate for consolidation, but it still fits the super-app strategy and is unlikely to be cut within a year.

The NFC tag authenticator is a niche hardware-dependent product with only a passing mention, so a firm facing pressure in a competitive market would likely redirect resources from it to the core platform as part of problemistic search.
The secure payment and wallet framework has its own page and is a central building block of the platform-business model, so it is likely meeting aspirations and will be kept.
The multi-service mobile app platform embodies the firm's strategic direction toward super apps, so dropping it would contradict the core identity of the firm.
The application shielding library has its own page and builds directly on the firm's decades of app-security expertise and patents, giving it a strong fit and low risk of being dropped.
